state.case_summary:
A woman in her 60s with a 20-year history of palpitations and shortness of breath. Episodes were previously controlled with verapamil but sustained symptoms recurred 6 months before presentation, not responding to amiodarone therapy.

- Heart rate: 122 beats per minute- Blood pressure: 135/85 mm Hg- Cardiovascular exam: Regular rhythm with cannon A waves in the jugular venous waveform

- ECG: Regular tachycardia at 130 beats per minute with incomplete right bundle branch block morphology, QRS duration of 118 milliseconds, and left-axis deviation. QRS complexes outnumber P waves with 3:2 relationship. P-wave morphology shows negative deflection in leads II and aVF.  Image Title: Figure 1A - Electrocardiographic Findings  Image Description: Regular relatively narrow-complex tachycardia with right bundle branch block and left-axis deviation. 3:2 relationship between ventricular and atrial activations.- 24-hour Holter monitor: Sustained tachycardia throughout monitoring period- Echocardiogram: Results within normal limits- Electrophysiology study: Confirmed origin of tachycardia

root.label: Chronic Progressive Cardiac Conduction Syndrome with Sustained Tachycardia of Uncertain Aetiology
supporting_facts: 20-year history of palpitations and shortness of breath
Sustained symptoms recurred 6 months before presentation, not responding to amiodarone therapy
Regular rhythm with cannon A waves in the jugular venous waveform
ECG: Regular tachycardia at 130 beats per minute with incomplete right bundle branch block morphology
excluded_candidates: Competing mechanism: Atrial fibrillation - excluded due to regular rhythm
Competing mechanism: Ventricular tachycardia - excluded due to narrow QRS complexes
salient_findings: Incomplete right bundle branch block morphology
P-wave morphology shows negative deflection in leads II and aVF
3:2 relationship between ventricular and atrial activations

B1.label: Tachycardia of Reentrant Origin
askable_discriminators: Is the tachycardia regular or irregular?
Is there a history of heart disease or previous cardiac procedures?

B2.label: Tachycardia of Automatic Origin
askable_discriminators: Is the tachycardia triggered by physical activity or emotional stress?
Is there a history of electrolyte imbalances or medication use?

B3.label: Cardiomyopathy-related Tachycardia
askable_discriminators: Is there a family history of cardiomyopathy or sudden cardiac death?
Are there symptoms of heart failure or reduced exercise tolerance?

B4.label: Other Cardiac Conditions
askable_discriminators: Are there symptoms of coronary artery disease or vasculitis?
Is there a history of cardiac surgery or intervention?
